subjects.term: MSC2020 51M20: Polyhedra and polytopes; regular figures, division of spaces

title: Equanimity: Fair Dice and the Regular Polygons Hidden in Their Vacuus
description:
Cut one Platonic or Catalan solid by another whose faces point along different symmetry axes, and let the second set of faces move out from the centre: one parameter μ runs a line of solids with two kinds of face. Twelve such lines have both face families along symmetry axes of the cube or the icosahedron, each family one orbit of the line's group; on each we find the member on which every face is equally likely, in the sense that it subtends the same solid angle 4π/N from the centre. These are fair dice with 10, 14, 16, 16, 18, 18, 20, 20, 24, 32, 42 and 50 faces, not face-transitive; four of them mix the cube's axes with the icosahedron's. Every fair member lies within 7% of the member whose faces all touch one sphere. For the 14-face die the values are exact: the cut is μ = 1 + √(2 tan(π/14) tan(2π/7)) in the cube's scale, and the ratio of inradius to circumradius is cot(2π/7). The dice with 20 and 32 faces have their radii in the fields of the regular 10-gon and 16-gon with √2 and √5; the 20-face die has (R/r)² = 11/3 + 2√2 − √5 − (2/3)√10, golden and silver together in a solid of cubic symmetry. The octahedron–dodecahedron die has R/r = 8 − 3√5. The dice with 10, 16 and 18 faces of the cubic lines have radii in no regular polygon's field. Yet ten of the twelve show a regular polygon in their Vacuus. Where one family of faces are regular m-gons, the plates through their edges and the centre meet the plane through the face's axis and corner at θ = π/2 − (N − 2)π/(mN): 7π/30, 2π/7, 5π/24, 5π/18, π/5, 5π/16, 13π/42 and 9π/50, a whole multiple of π/N, or of π/3N on the lines with a tetrahedron. We prove this by hand from Girard's theorem; the two dice without regular faces show no such angle. The proof gives these ten dice in closed form, μf = b·a + (b·u)·√(tan²(π/m) tan²θ − 1); on the octahedron–rhombic dodecahedron line μf = (2√2 + 3 − √5)/(2√3).

Builds on DICTO Vacuus Solids (#87, DICTO DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23896015) and The Golden Ladder (DICTO DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23966554, Chapter 3A, §5.4).

Computation, proofs, verification and drafting with Claude (Anthropic).
